reason: The cited evidence directly shows that a 10.2 at.% Al coating on N36 zirconium alloy forms a dense Nb2Zr6O17/ZrO2 oxide layer and exhibits the best corrosion resistance and lowest oxygen penetration, supporting the core premises. However, the evidence is from corrosion testing under PWR operational conditions, not high-temperature steam oxidation simulating LOCA, so the premise that this mechanism holds under accident conditions is not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: AlNbTiZr MEA coatings with ~10 at.% Al form a dense oxide layer of Nb2Zr6O17 and ZrO2
This oxide layer gives the best corrosion resistance and minimum oxygen penetration depth among tested Al contents
The coating is applied on a zirconium-alloy substrate relevant to PWR cladding
The coating's performance was evaluated under conditions relevant to PWR operation
